'''Myles Robert Allen''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|CBE|FRS|FInstP}} (born 11 August 1965)<ref name=whoswho/> is an English climate scientist. He is Professor of Geosystem Science in the [[University of Oxford]]'s 
[[School of Geography and the Environment, University of Oxford|
School of Geography and the Environment]], and head of the Atmospheric, Oceanic and Planetary Physics Department.<ref name="CV">{{cite web |url=http://www.ox.ac.uk/research/mathematical_physical_life_sciences/people/dr_myles_allen.html |title=Dr Myles Allen - University of Oxford |access-date=2010-01-12 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091230134122/http://www.ox.ac.uk/research/mathematical_physical_life_sciences/people/dr_myles_allen.html |archive-date=2009-12-30 }} Myles Allen profile at the University of Oxford</ref><ref>''[[The Guardian]]'' articles by Allen: [https://www.theguardian.com/profile/myles-r-allen Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change must keep its eye on the ball]; [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/cif-green/2009/apr/29/climate-change-research-myles-allen Generals must give us their exit strategy for climate change]</ref>

==Education==
Allen was educated at the [[British School in the Netherlands]]<ref name=whoswho/> and the [[University of Oxford]] where he was awarded a [[Master of Arts]] degree in [[physics]] and [[philosophy]] in 1987<ref name=whoswho/> followed by a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree in 1992.<ref name=PhD>{{cite thesis|degree=DPhil|publisher=University of Oxford|url=https://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/permalink/f/89vilt/oxfaleph015949185|title=Interactions between the atmosphere and oceans on time scales of weeks to years|first= Myles Robert|last=Allen|date=1992|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.335863}}|website=ox.ac.uk|oclc=61666921}}</ref> He was a student of [[St. John's College, Oxford]].<ref name=whoswho/>

==Career==

Allen has worked at the Energy Unit of the [[United Nations Environment Programme]], the [[Rutherford Appleton Laboratory]] in Oxfordshire, and the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref name="CV"/>

Allen also provided the technical expertise for the game ''Fate of the World'', which is "a PC strategy game that simulates the real social and environmental impact of global climate change over the next 200 years".<ref>{{cite web| url=http://fateoftheworld.net/about | title=About Fate of the World | date=4 March 2011 | website=fateoftheworld.net/about | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110304212304/http://fateoftheworld.net/about | archive-date=2011-03-04 }}</ref>
In 2015, he mentioned that [[carbon capture and storage]] (CCS) should be made mandatory.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2015/jul/02/fossil-fuel-companies-should-be-made-to-invest-in-carbon-capture-and-storage | title=Fossil fuel companies 'should be made to invest in carbon capture and storage' | newspaper=[[The Guardian]] | date=2 July 2015 }}</ref>

== Awards and honours ==
In 2010, Allen was awarded the [[Edward Appleton Medal and Prize]] by the [[Institute of Physics]] for "his important contributions to the detection and attribution of human influence on climate and quantifying uncertainty in climate predictions".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iop.org/about/awards/subject/appleton/medallists/page_38521.html|title=Appleton medal recipients|publisher=Institute of Physics|page=1|access-date=26 August 2010}}</ref>
Allen was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the [[2022 New Year Honours]] for services to climate change attribution and prediction and net-zero.<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=63571|supp=y|page=N8|date=1 January 2022}}</ref> He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Myles Allen |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/myles-allen-36203/ |access-date=2023-05-26 |website=royalsociety.org}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Allen married [[Irene Tracey]] in 1994 and has three children.<ref name=whoswho/>
